key_insight: PXRD-Bench shows that PXRD-to-structure models are improving, but robust structure recovery still breaks down on unseen chemistries, new prototypes, and two-phase mixtures.
engineering_relevance: This benchmark moves PXRD analysis closer to routine materials characterization by testing whether models can infer crystal structures from realistic experimental diffraction data, not just idealized single-phase cases.
method: Built PXRD-Bench with ~4.1M simulated training structures.
Evaluated generalization to unseen compositions, unseen structural prototypes, and two-phase mixtures.
Introduced Bragglite as a strong PXRD-to-structure baseline and systematically studied PXRD modeling choices.
evidence_signal: Bragglite reached 44.2% Top-1 match on experimental RRUFF patterns with known composition, 24.6 percentage points above the previous best baseline, while harder benchmark settings remained challenging.
watch_item: Performance on experimental data may not transfer reliably to unseen prototypes or mixed-phase samples, so benchmark gains should be interpreted cautiously for real-world deployment.
paper_title: PXRD-Bench: How Close Are We to Determining Crystal Structures from Powder Diffraction?
